City of La Habra Heights
  AGENDA REPORT
  Meeting Date: December 2, 2019

  Agenda Item # _9__

TO:  Roads Advisory Committee

FROM:  Fabiola Huerta, City Manager

SUBJECT:  PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT PROGRAM 2019-2024 FINAL REPORT
  PRESENTATION (CONTINUED FROM 10/28/2019)

BACKGROUND

At the October 28, 2019 Roads Advisory Committee meeting, Peter Bucknam presented
the Pavement Management Program 2019-2024 final report. The Committee requested
updates to the report and also had a discussion with Mr. Bucknam regarding preventative
maintenance and the inclusion of drainage in the PMP. Mr. Bucknam and the City
Engineer will be present at the December 2, 2019 meeting to answer questions.

At the time of writing this staff report, a revision of the PMP was not available. The report
will be uploaded as soon as it is received.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Roads Advisory Committee recommend that the City Council
approve and adopt the Pavement Management Program 2019-2024 Final Report.
   City of La Habra Heights
  AGENDA REPORT
  Meeting Date: December 2, 2019

  Agenda Item # _10_

TO:  Roads Advisory Committee

FROM:  Fabiola Huerta, City Manager

SUBJECT:  HACIENDA ROAD UPDATE

BACKGROUND

The final geotechnical report and the design of the Phase 1 repair was submitted to the
City on October 29, 2019. There was a change in the scope of work for the Phase 1
repair. Instead of grading to a depth of 8 to 10 feet, the plans changed the grading depth
to 13 feet. By expanding the scope of Phase 1, there is a potential of significantly reducing
the scope of work and costs of the Phase 2 repair.

On November 6, 2019, the City and GMU met with resident John Smith. Mr. Smith
provided information on alternate methodologies for re-constructing the pavement. GMU
performed additional value engineering, taking into consideration Mr. Smith’s information,
and as a result, provided alternate scope items to the contractors. Due to the alternate
scope, a savings of approximately $48,000 in costs was seen for the project. At the
November 12, 2019 City Council meeting, the City Council awarded the contract to Earth
Construction & Mining for a total of $366,212.43.

Below is information on the current status of Hacienda Road. From the current draft 2019
Pavement Management Program, the nine sections of Hacienda Road are listed as
having the following PCIs and the assigned strategies:

 From  To  PCI  Strategy Assigned
 South City Limit  Avocado Crest Road  87  Preventative, Stop Gap,
  Patching
 Avocado Crest Road  West Road  70  Type II Slurry Seal
 West Road  East Road  79  Type II Slurry Seal
 East Road  Encanada Drive  71  Type II Slurry Seal
 Encanada Drive  Reposado Drive  69  Grind and Overlay
 Reposado Drive  Canada Sombre Road  77  Type II Slurry Seal
 Canada Sombre Road  Skyline Drive  67  Grind and Overlay
  Skyline Drive  636’ N/O Skyline Drive  87  Preventative, Stop Gap,
  Patching
 636’ N/O Skyline Drive  North City Limit  87  Preventative, Stop Gap,
  Patching

Staff requested a proposal from Los Angeles County to crack seal Hacienda Road and
the estimate was $30,000. Staff has also received complaints from residents who live on
the North end of Hacienda Road that the slurry has significantly deteriorated in the area
North of Skyline Drive, which has caused an increase in the noise level when cars drive
on that portion of the road.

At this time, staff is asking the Committee to provide recommendations on possible
improvements of Hacienda Road to the City Council. The information will be presented to
the City Council at the December 9, 2019 meeting.

FISCAL IMPACT

There is no fiscal impact with the discussion of this item.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Roads Advisory Committee discuss and provide a
recommendation to the City Council.
   City of La Habra Heights
  AGENDA REPORT
  Meeting Date: December 2, 2019

  Agenda Item # _11_

TO:  Roads Advisory Committee

FROM:  Fabiola Huerta, City Manager

SUBJECT:  CRACK SEAL PROJECT

This item was requested by Committee Member Pedersen.

BACKGROUND

Questions and recommendations regarding crack sealing from Committee Member
Pedersen include:

  1. If the approach for grind and overlay is the same for the 2019-2020 project, as it
  was for the 2018-2019, then cracks will be filled after the overlay segments have
  been grinded (please confirm this understanding and let me know).

  2. Also, please confirm that crack fill beyond the overlay segments has not been
  specified by the plans/specs or included in the bid (making it extra work).

  3. If my understanding is correct on items 1 & 2, then we are essentially already
  paying for the mobilization to get the crack fill sub on the job for the overlay
  segments. It would seem to me that we may have an opportunity to economically
  crack fill on the rest of the zone if the sub is amenable to giving us a good price.
  We should at least explore this possibility.

  4. In future projects, I would strongly suggest we crack fill the entire zone as part of
  the project or at a minimum include an alternate bid item to do so. By including it
  up front as part of the project, the contractor will have incentive to minimize the
  cost in order to keep the bid low. If it is included as an alternate item, then we need
  to spell out that we may choose the low bidder based on a combination of the base
  bid and the alternate items (in order to make sure we are getting a competitive
  price). I would love to see this recommended in the PMP (but only if Buckman
  agrees at a planning level).

  5. Until we find an economical approach to crack fill, I would emphasize the need
  follow the recommendations presented in items 3 & 4.
 Peter Bucknam and the City Engineer will be available at the December 2, 2019 meeting
to answer questions and provide recommendations.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Roads Advisory Committee discuss and provide direction to
staff.
